A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same embedding-plus-MLP forecasting work, renamed from LightWeather to STELLA. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial revision.

before.justification: V1 reports original forecasting experiments on five datasets, embedding ablations, hyperparameter studies, and efficiency measurements.

after.justification: V2 reports original forecasting experiments, ablations, CPU measurements, embedding-transfer experiments, and comparative prediction cases, including results in its appendices.

M1.justification: The spatial encoder changes from a single fully connected layer in v1 Eq. (3) to a two-layer ReLU feed-forward network in v2 Eq. (3). This is a limited architectural revision: additive calendar embeddings, the residual MLP backbone, and the forecasting head remain.

E1.justification: GlobalWind and GlobalTemp remain, while Wind_CN and Temp_CN become ChinaWind and ChinaTemp. The 27-station Wind_US benchmark is removed and replaced by the reported ChinaPM2.5 air-quality task covering 1,316 Chinese stations, substantially changing the represented population and target domain.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds AGCRN, MTGNN, GTS, iTransformer, DUET, N-BEATS, and FITS, while removing TimesNet, GPT4TS, and Time-LLM. The embedding-transfer comparison in Table 4 also replaces MRIformer with iTransformer, although MRIformer remains in the main comparison.

E3.justification: V1 specifies 48 input and 24 forecast steps throughout; v2 changes the retained Chinese weather tasks to 60/30 and introduces 72/72 for air quality, retaining 48/24 globally. Main evaluation changes from MSE/MAE to RMSE/MAE. V2 also evaluates separate STELLA-10k and optimized configurations and adds a CPU training/inference protocol.

E4.justification: V2 newly tests whether STPE benefits DLinear (Appendix E.3), adds comparative station-level cases (Figures 9–11), and examines the geographic distribution of embedding clusters (Figure 5). Existing embedding-removal and relative-position ablations expand from two global datasets to all five datasets.

E5.justification: Both versions report five-run means and standard deviations for the proposed model's main results. However, v2 removes v1 Table 2's explicit statement that efficiency measurements were averaged over three runs. This is reduced repetition disclosure, without evidence that the actual run count decreased.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds separate STELLA-10k/STELLAopt results and new comparator and ChinaPM2.5 scores, while removing Wind_US results. GlobalWind MAE changes from 1.295 for LightWeather to 1.294/1.284 for the two STELLA configurations; their differing models and settings prevent treating these as controlled performance gains. Tables 8–10 add CPU, lightweight-efficiency, and linear-transfer outcomes.

T1.justification: Theorem 1 gains explicit dependence on the atmospheric state. V1's scalar corollary is replaced by a multi-step formulation with a history-dependent residual and a matrix-norm condition. Appendix A adds a full atmospheric-equation derivation, rewrites the corollary proof, and revises the parameter-count theorem and proof.

C1.justification: The central application claim broadens from station-based weather forecasting to atmospheric time series forecasting, including air quality. V2 newly claims the first lightweight model designed for ATSF and distinguishes competitive STELLA-10k performance from optimized-model superiority. The underlying claim that spatial-temporal knowledge can substitute for complex architectures remains.

C2.justification: V2 adds substantive limitations concerning neglected multivariate coupling, overly smooth extreme-event forecasts, and limited MLP capacity (Section 5 and Appendix G). Appendix E explains limited gains for linear models and distinguishes input-based physical priors from PINN constraints. These substantially extend v1's brief discussion of future physical integration.

D1.justification: V2 adds a code-repository pointer and Table 6's dataset-specific dimensions, layer counts, epochs, dropout, weight decay, and learning-rate schedules. It newly documents coordinate normalization and baseline loss/search practices, and updates software and hardware disclosures. Conversely, v1's explicit 7:1:2 training/validation/test split statement disappears.

R1.justification: V2 expands positioning and citations around graph models, lightweight forecasters, attention alternatives such as SOFTS, and physics-informed approaches. Appendix E.2 introduces an explicit novelty distinction from PINNs. V1's discussion of gridded radar/reanalysis methods and references associated with removed TimesNet and language-model baselines are dropped.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, terminology, and contribution narrative are substantially rewritten around ATSF and STELLA/STPE. The methodology is reorganized, visualization and case-study material are reordered, and existing appendix content is redistributed alongside new discussion and limitations sections.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column formatting. Architecture and mechanism diagrams are redrawn, comparison tables are restructured, and the embedding visualization gains a geographic panel. New proof diagrams, configuration/efficiency tables, and station-level plots are added; the existing global forecast maps are retained and renumbered.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens the accuracy-efficiency argument by testing relevant graph and lightweight alternatives and directly measuring CPU operation, addressing important gaps in v1's validation. Detailed configurations and explicit failure limitations also make the work easier to assess and reproduce. These gains outweigh reporting regressions: the split ratio and efficiency repetition count disappear, and Table 7 retains MSE labels although its numerical-method values are square roots of v1's MSE values. The improvement rests on stronger validation and transparency, not simply broader claims or lower reported errors.
